name: Mushroom Masala
cuisine: North Indian (Punjabi-style dhaba and home curry)

ingredients.name: Ginger-garlic paste (adrak-lahsun)
ingredients.householdMeasure: 1½ tsp (or 1 tsp each of grated ginger and garlic)

equipment: Kadai or deep frying pan with a lid (8–9 inch)
Kitchen towel or paper towel to dry the mushrooms
Small bowl and fork or spoon to whisk the curd
No kadai? Any heavy-bottomed pan or a wide saucepan works

steps.title: Clean the mushrooms
steps.text: Put the 200 g mushrooms in a colander and rinse them quickly under running water, rubbing off any dirt with your fingers.
steps.tip: Don't soak them; mushrooms absorb water like a sponge and then turn soggy in the curry.
steps.visualCue: White caps with no black soil specks.
steps.cameraCheck: The rinsed mushrooms in the colander
steps.videoShot: Hands rubbing mushrooms under a running tap.

steps.title: Dry them
steps.text: Spread the mushrooms on a kitchen towel and pat them dry.
steps.visualCue: Caps look matte, with no water drops.
steps.videoShot: A towel pressing gently on the mushrooms.

steps.title: Trim and slice the mushrooms
steps.text: Cut a thin slice off the bottom of each stem, then cut each mushroom into 4–5 mm thick slices (or quarter small ones).
steps.tip: Throw away any mushroom that is slimy or smells sour. Slightly brown gills are fine.
steps.visualCue: Even slices with the stem attached, white inside with no dark, slimy spots.
steps.cameraCheck: The sliced mushrooms on the board
steps.videoShot: A knife slicing a mushroom into even slices.

steps.title: Chop the tomato
steps.tip: For a smoother restaurant-style gravy, blend the tomato to a purée instead.
steps.visualCue: Small pieces with their juice on the board.

steps.title: Prep the chilli, coriander and curd
steps.text: Slit the green chilli lengthwise, chop 2 tbsp coriander leaves, and whisk 2 tbsp curd in a small bowl with a fork until smooth.
steps.tip: Take the curd out of the fridge first; cold curd splits more easily in hot gravy.
steps.visualCue: The curd is smooth and lump-free.
steps.cameraCheck: The slit chilli, coriander and whisked curd
steps.videoShot: A fork whisking curd in a small bowl.

steps.title: Heat the oil
steps.text: Put the kadai on medium heat and add 1 tbsp oil.
steps.visualCue: The oil shimmers and flows easily when you tilt the pan.
steps.videoShot: Oil being poured into a kadai.

steps.title: Temper the cumin and bay leaf
steps.text: Add ½ tsp cumin seeds and the bay leaf.
steps.visualCue: The cumin sizzles and darkens one shade; it smells toasty.
steps.cameraCheck: The cumin and bay leaf sizzling
steps.videoShot: Cumin seeds crackling around a bay leaf.

steps.title: Fry the onion
steps.text: Add the chopped onion and stir on medium heat.
steps.tip: Golden (not just soft) onion gives the gravy its depth and colour. If it starts catching, add 1 tsp water.
steps.visualCue: The onion is soft and evenly golden brown at the edges.
steps.cameraCheck: The golden onion in the kadai
steps.videoShot: The spatula stirring onion as it turns golden.

steps.title: Add the ginger-garlic paste and green chilli
steps.visualCue: The raw garlic smell is gone and the pan smells fragrant.
steps.cameraCheck: The onion with the paste mixed in
steps.videoShot: Ginger-garlic paste going into the onions.

steps.title: Add the spice powders
steps.text: Turn the heat to low and add ⅛ tsp turmeric, ½ tsp Kashmiri chilli powder and ¾ tsp coriander powder. Stir.
steps.tip: Low heat stops the powders burning. If the pan looks dry, add 1 tsp water.
steps.visualCue: The onion is evenly coated orange-red and smells spicy; nothing is burning.

steps.title: Cook the tomato
steps.text: Add the chopped tomato and ⅓ tsp salt, turn the heat to medium and cook, pressing the tomato with the spatula.
steps.visualCue: The tomato breaks down into a thick, jammy masala and a little oil shines at the edges.
steps.videoShot: The spatula mashing tomato into a thick masala.

steps.title: Add the curd
steps.text: Turn the heat to low, add the whisked curd and stir continuously.
steps.tip: Keep stirring and keep the heat low; high heat makes curd split into grains.
steps.visualCue: The curd blends in completely and the masala looks creamy and orange, with no white specks.
steps.videoShot: Whisked curd being stirred into the masala.

steps.title: Add the mushrooms
steps.text: Add all the sliced mushrooms, turn the heat to medium-high and stir to coat them in the masala.
steps.tip: Don't add the water until the mushrooms have released their own; they make most of the gravy.
steps.visualCue: The mushrooms shrink and release their water; the pan looks juicy.
steps.videoShot: Mushroom slices being tossed in the red masala.

steps.title: Add water and simmer covered
steps.text: Pour in 60 ml water, stir, cover and simmer on low-medium heat.
steps.tip: Want it thicker? Cook uncovered for 2 more min. Thinner? Add 2–3 tbsp hot water. Taste and adjust salt now.
steps.visualCue: The mushrooms are soft but still hold their shape, and the gravy has thickened to coat a spoon.
steps.cameraCheck: The simmering curry with the lid lifted
steps.videoShot: The lid lifted to show a bubbling mushroom gravy.

steps.title: Finish with garam masala and kasuri methi
steps.text: Crush 1 tsp kasuri methi between your palms over the pan, add ¼ tsp garam masala and stir.
steps.visualCue: A sweet, fragrant smell from the methi; flecks of green in the gravy.
steps.cameraCheck: The kasuri methi being crushed over the pan
steps.videoShot: Palms rubbing dried methi over the curry.

steps.title: Add coriander and switch off
steps.text: Sprinkle the chopped coriander, stir once and switch off the heat. Remove the bay leaf.
steps.visualCue: Bright green flecks over a glossy, orange-brown gravy.
steps.cameraCheck: The finished curry in the kadai
steps.videoShot: Coriander scattered over the mushroom masala.

steps.title: Serve
steps.visualCue: Soft mushroom slices in a thick, glossy, orange-brown gravy.
steps.videoShot: Mushroom masala spooned into a bowl beside a hot roti.

reasons: a low-calorie vegetable curry (about 260 kcal) with about 6 g fibre, good potassium, selenium and B vitamins from the mushrooms, only 1 tbsp of oil and very little saturated fat. Points come off for modest protein (about 10 g, so it needs dal, curd or paneer alongside to be a full meal) and for sodium at about 41% of the daily limit. Restaurant versions commonly use 2–3 tbsp oil and finish with butter, cream or cashew paste, which can double the calories and raise saturated fat.

researchRating.basis: a popular everyday North Indian curry with very well-reviewed recipes (Indian Healthy Recipes, mushroom curry / mushroom masala, 4.96/5 from 301 votes; Hebbar's Kitchen, mushroom masala, 5/5 from 45 votes on the main page, though a print copy shows 3/5 from 2 votes; Whisk Affair 5/5 from 1 vote), and it is a standard item on Punjabi restaurant menus. Deduction because mushrooms are a polarising ingredient (texture and earthy taste), and many home cooks report watery or rubbery results when the mushrooms are overcooked.

storage: Refrigerate in an airtight box within 2 hours of cooking. It keeps for 1–2 days in the fridge (est.); mushrooms soften and release more water the longer they sit. Freezing is not recommended: the mushrooms turn spongy and rubbery and the curd gravy can split after thawing. To reheat, warm it in a pan on low-medium heat for 2–3 min, stirring gently (don't boil hard, or the curd may split), or microwave covered for 1–1½ min, stirring halfway. Reheat only once.
leftoverRemix: Mushroom masala frankie. Cook the leftover curry in a dry pan for 2–3 min until the gravy clings to the mushrooms and is almost dry. Spread a little green chutney on a warm roti, add the mushrooms, a few raw onion rings and a pinch of chaat masala, roll it up tightly and toast it seam-side down on a tawa for 1 min.
burnOff: about 3.7 km of running (260 ÷ 70 kcal/km, for a 70 kg adult), or about 5.2 km of brisk walking (about 1 h at 5 km/h, using about 50 kcal/km for walking) (est.). This is for the mushroom masala alone; 2 phulkas would add about 2–2.5 km of running.

navratri.reason: contains onion, garlic and regular table salt (assumption: common North Indian vrat rules, which avoid all three)

ekadashi.reason: contains onion and garlic, which most Ekadashi observers avoid

jain.reason: mushrooms (fungi) are forbidden in the Jain diet, and onion, garlic and ginger are roots

ramadan.reason: vegetarian, light (about 260 kcal) and fairly high in fibre; for sehri keep the salt moderate and pair it with roti and dal or curd so the meal has more protein and lasts longer

jain.reason: mushrooms are fungi, which Jain dietary rules forbid (to avoid harming small life and because fungi grow in unclean conditions); the recipe also uses onion, garlic and fresh ginger (roots)

vegan.reason: replace the 30 g curd with 30 ml thick coconut milk (see Vegan variant)

pescatarian.reason: contains no meat or poultry; a vegetarian dish fits a pescatarian diet

sattvik.reason: skip the onion and garlic and build the gravy on extra tomato and a little cashew (see Sattvik variant); note that some sattvik households avoid mushrooms themselves, a rule not confirmed in this run's sources

glutenFree.reason: no wheat, rava or maida, and no hing in this recipe (if you add hing, most hing sold in India is compounded with wheat flour)

dairyFree.reason: the curd (30 g) is the only dairy; use thick coconut milk instead (restaurant versions often also add butter and cream)

description: A vegetarian, gluten-free North Indian mushroom curry, not suitable for Jains (fungi); vegan, dairy-free, no-onion-no-garlic and low-oil versions below.

variants.reason: mushrooms are the base of the dish, and fungi are forbidden in the Jain diet (Wikipedia, Jain vegetarianism). Swapping them out (e.g. for paneer or capsicum) makes a different dish; choose a Jain sabzi instead.
main recipe already Gluten-free (no wheat, rava, maida or hing).
